svg.title: DSCP to switch priority to eight egress queues, including the NVIDIA Cumulus RoCE preset
svg.desc: The upper section shows eight default DSCP classification buckets mapping to switch priorities zero through seven and then to eight identically numbered base egress queues. The lower section shows the RoCE preset remapping all priorities except three and six to queue zero, while priority three maps to RoCE queue three and priority six maps to strict-priority CNP queue six. A clarification states that CS3 is exactly DSCP 24, not the entire 24 through 31 bucket.
svg.text: Default trusted-DSCP classification and base identity mapping versus the NVIDIA Cumulus RoCE preset

g.text: RoCE preset: only Q0 / Q3 / Q6 active

svg.text: BASE / DEFAULT CLASSIFICATION WHEN L3 DSCP IS TRUSTED

g.text: Base Cumulus QoS supports all eight egress queues and maps each trusted switch priority to the identically numbered queue.

svg.text: ROCE PRESET: EIGHT SWITCH PRIORITIES COLLAPSE INTO THREE ACTIVE EGRESS QUEUES

g.text: All non-RoCE and non-CNP priorities are remapped here.
Payload shares the link by weight.
Fast feedback; “6” does not imply rank.
Strict is an explicit scheduler mode—not a property of queue number 6.
CS3 = binary 011000 = decimal 24. The whole 24–31 bucket maps to SP3,
RoCE queue choices are profile defaults
Trust mode, ACLs, and platform QoS policy can override classification and queues.
Q7 does not preempt Q6 here; SP7 is remapped to shared Q0.

svg.text: Sources: NVIDIA Cumulus Linux QoS and RoCE default profiles · IANA DSCP Registry · RFC 2474 / RFC 9435
Illustrative profile · verify the live switch configuration before deployment
